name: DIY, Wait or Call a Pro
why_it_works: A pro who tells viewers which problems they can fix themselves sounds honest, not salesy. Giving away the easy fix first makes the one item that truly needs {{brand}} believable, and the three-bucket sort is simple enough to remember and save.

hook.pattern: Promise to sort common problems into three buckets: fix it yourself, let it wait, or call a pro now.
examples: DIY, wait, or call a pro? Three {{profession}} problems.
Fix it, ignore it, or call? A {{profession}} sorts it.
Three problems, three buckets. Only one needs me.

variables.name: profession
variables.description: The trade, in plain words; 2 words or fewer

variables.name: diy_item
variables.description: A common problem viewers can safely fix themselves; 5 words or fewer

variables.name: diy_fix
variables.description: The quick fix, read after "Just"; starts with a verb, 6 words or fewer

variables.name: wait_item
variables.description: A problem that looks scary but can safely wait and be watched; 6 words or fewer
variables.example: a squeaky belt on cold mornings

variables.name: call_item
variables.description: The problem that needs a pro now; 5 words or fewer

variables.name: call_reason
variables.description: Why it cannot wait, read after "because"; 5 words or fewer

variables.name: offer
variables.description: Low-risk next step; 6 words or fewer
variables.example: a free brake check this week

beats.on_screen_text: DIY, wait, or call a pro?
beats.voiceover: Three {{profession}} problems: DIY, wait, or call?

visual.prompt: Three labeled bins on a {{brand}} workbench reading DIY, WAIT and CALL, bright even light, centered framing, vertical 9:16

beats.purpose: bucket 1: the easy fix the viewer can do

visual.prompt: Close-up of everyday hands doing a simple at-home fix related to {{diy_item}}, green DIY tag in the corner, natural light, vertical

beats.purpose: bucket 2: the scary-looking thing that can wait
beats.voiceover: It can wait: {{wait_item}}. Watch it, don't panic.

beats.purpose: bucket 3: the one that needs a pro, shown in motion

visual.prompt: Slow push-in on the source of {{call_item}} in a {{brand}} work bay, red CALL tag sliding into frame, tense practical light, vertical 9:16

beats.voiceover: Not sure which bucket? Ask {{brand}} first.

visual.prompt: A {{profession}} at the {{brand}} counter listening to a customer, relaxed, warm window light, vertical 9:16

cta: Not sure which bucket? Start with {{offer}}.

craft.notes: Three items, three buckets, always in the order DIY, wait, call. Giving away a real free fix first earns the right to say one thing is urgent. The call item must be genuinely urgent, or the whole sort reads as a sales trick.

do_not: Put anything unsafe or license-only in the DIY bucket
Make every item a call-a-pro item; the sort only works if two of three are free
Exaggerate the danger of the call item to scare viewers into booking
compliance: Dental: no diagnosis in the ad; the call-a-pro item invites a consultation, and DIY items stay within everyday home care
Healthcare providers: no claims of cures or guaranteed results, and no patient images without written consent
